subject: Data handling & access controls follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintrust.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T18:12:00Z
Subject: Data handling & access controls follow-up

Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery focused on data handling, privacy, and access controls plus proposed next steps: 

1) Recap of customer requirements you called out:
- PII scope: customer emails and small set of user identifiers (no SSNs or financial detail at this stage)
- Data residency: must remain in US (prefer us-east-1)
- Retention: default 90 days for customer logs/outputs, ability to configure retention shorter on request
- Audit/logging: immutable audit trail for all support/admin actions, access logs retained for one year (configurable)
- Access controls: RBAC, least-privilege roles for developers vs. support, and a documented break-glass procedure with immediate audit and notification to your security team

2) What Redwood confirmed on the call:
- Hosted API supports region pinning to AWS us-east-1 and we can offer a Private deployment for stricter isolation if needed
- RBAC: role-based model + SSO (SAML/OIDC) integrations; fine-grained roles for read/write/admin on model endpoints
- Support access: ephemeral, time-bound break-glass keys; all support sessions are recorded and audited; customer-managed KMS support for key encryption
- Data retention: configurable at account or route level; default logs retention policy is 90 days, audit logs kept 1 year unless otherwise requested

3) Outstanding questions / asks from FinTrust for next steps:
- Can you confirm whether the retention defaults (90d logs, 1y audit) meet your policy or whether you need shorter retention?
- Please share a copy of any internal security questionnaire you want us to fill (we have a fillable version attached)
- Would you like a technical deep-dive with Rishi (solutions engineering) to walk through RBAC, break-glass, and log exports?

4) Proposed next steps:
- I can book a 45-min session with Rishi + Vivek next week to walk through the technical controls and attach our evidence pack (attached).
- If helpful, we can also produce a short write-up showing exactly which data fields are persisted for the endpoints you plan to call.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning on these items. If you want to loop in your security lead now, please do and I’ll include them on the follow-up invite.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintrust.com>

Date: 2026-08-30T20:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Data handling & access controls follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. Confirming a few items from our side and a couple of asks before we schedule the tech call:

- Retention: our default policy for the project team is 90 days for application logs. We have a 6-month limit for audit logs, but shorter is acceptable if you can provide guarantees for secure deletion. Please clarify deletion process and proof of deletion for data at rest.
- PII: as noted, limited to emails and a hashed user_id. No direct identifiers beyond email. We need confirmation that payloads stored in any caches or logs will not include unmasked PII.
- Break-glass: we require a documented procedure that includes immediate notification to our security ops, time-limited elevated access, and post-access review.

Can you also attach your SOC 2 report or point me to an evidence summary? Priya (cc) is our security manager and will review. If you can send the evidence pack and the fillable questionnaire back today, we’ll kick off an internal review.

Assuming those look good, we’d like the technical session — Tue or Wed next week (your availability?). Prefer a hour block where Priya can join.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
FinTrust
alex.johnson@fintrust.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T13:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Data handling & access controls follow-up (technical answers)

Marissa / Vivek — adding a few technical clarifications you can pass to FinTrust: 

1) RBAC / least privilege:
- We support hierarchy-based roles: Viewer, Developer, Operator, Admin. Roles can be scoped to projects, model routes, or resources (buckets, endpoints).
- SAML/OIDC SSO: SCIM provisioning available for automated user lifecycle.
- Fine-grained policy language available to block export of certain fields (we can add masking rules for email fields at ingestion if requested).

2) Support access / break-glass:
- Break-glass is implemented via ephemeral, one-time elevated session tokens issued through our support portal. Each session requires an explicit justification, TTL (recommended 30 minutes) and must be approved by on-call support manager.
- All break-glass sessions stream session logs (keystroke-level metadata + API call audit) to an immutable audit store. Notifications are emitted to configured webhooks (customer-managed) and to our security ops channel.
- We can integrate with customer SIEM/Syslog for real-time forwarding of audit events.

3) Logging & retention / deletion:
- Request logs and system audit logs are written to a write-once object store. Deletion requests are executed by a background job that marks objects for deletion and purges according to retention policy; we can provide deletion receipts and a manifest for compliance requests.
- Default behavior: request data in cache is short-lived (ephemeral KV cache) and not written to long-term storage unless you enable persistence for debugging.

4) Data residency & encryption:
- We support region pinning for hosted accounts and offer a Private deployment if you require customer-managed network boundaries.
- Data at rest encryption: AES-256 with customer-managed KMS available (bring-your-own-key).

Attachments I recommend we send: redwood-security-evidence-summary.pdf (SOC2 highlights + control mappings), architecture diagram (high level), and the fillable questionnaire.

Happy to join the technical session. My availability Tue/Wed next week 10:00-14:00 ET.

—Rishi
